ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AD \perp BC$ at point $D$, $BE \perp AC$ at point $E$, and $BE$ intersects $AD$ at point $F$. If $AD=BD=5$ and $CD=3$, what is the length of $AF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $BE\perp AC$ and $AD\perp BC$,\\
it follows that $\angle AEB=\angle ADC=\angle BDF=90^\circ$,\\
Given $\angle AFE=\angle BFD$ and $\angle FBD+\angle BDF+\angle BFD=180^\circ$, $\angle AEB+\angle AFE+\angle DAC=180^\circ$,\\
it implies $\angle DAC=\angle DBF$,\\
In $\triangle BDF$ and $\triangle ADC$, we have\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle DBF=\angle DAC\\
BD=AD\\
\angle BDF=\angle ADC
\end{array}\right.$,\\
which leads to $\triangle BDF \cong \triangle ADC\left(ASA\right)$,\\
thus $DF=CD=3$,\\
Since $AF+DF=AD=5$,\\
it results in $AF=\boxed{2}$.
